questions.question: A father was twelve times as old as his son twenty years ago. Now he is twice as old as his son. What are the present ages of the son and father?
questions.questionHtml: A father was twelve times as old as his son twenty years ago. Now he is twice as old as his son. What are the present ages of the son and father?
questions.solution:
Current age of Father = F; Son = S

F = 2S

Twenty years ago:

(F - 20) = 12 (S - 20)

F = 12S + 20 - 240

F = 12S - 220

2S = 12S - 220

10S = 220

Therefore, S = 22 and F = 44

Hence, the present ages of the son and father are 22 and 44 years respectively.

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 16 + 3 – 5 × 2 ÷ 4 = 9

questions.solution:
Let’s check the options one by one,

1) ÷ and + → 16 ÷ 3 – 5 × 2 + 4 ≠ 9

2) × and – → 16 + 3 × 5 – 2 ÷ 4 ≠ 9

3) × and + → 16 × 3 – 5 + 2 ÷ 4 ≠ 9

4) ÷ and × →16 + 3 – 5 ÷ 2 × 4 = 9

Hence, ‘÷ and ×’ is the correct answer.

questions.question: In economic terms what do we mean by 'intermediate goods'?
questions.questionHtml: In economic terms what do we mean by 'intermediate goods'?

options.text: Goods sold between industries for the resale or production of other goods
options.html: Goods sold between industries for the resale or production of other goods

options.text: Goods in transit before reaching the consumers
options.html: Goods in transit before reaching the consumers

questions.solution: Intermediate good is a product used to produce a final or finished product, also known as a consumer good. Intermediate goods are the goods sold between industries for the resale or production of other goods. These products are also called semi-finished products because they are used as inputs to become part of the finished products.

questions.question: Which of the following is the third stage in the metamorphosis of a butterﬂy?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the third stage in the metamorphosis of a butterﬂy?
questions.solution:
The first stage is the egg.

The Butterfly eggs are laid on the plants by the female Butterfly.

The second stage is the larva stage in which the butterfly exists in the form of a caterpillar.

The Third stage is Pupa which is transitional phase in which the Caterpillar changes into Butterfly.

The fourth stage is the Adult stage in which a full grown adult butterfly comes out of the pupa.

questions.solution:
⇒ x – 5√x – 1 = 0

Divide by √x

⇒ √x – 5 – 1/√x = 0

⇒ √x – 1/√x = 5

Squaring both the sides

⇒ (√x – 1/√x)2 = 52

⇒ x + 1/x – 2 = 25

⇒ x + 1/x = 27

Squaring both the sides again

⇒ (x + 1/x)2 = 272

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 + 2 = 729

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 727

questions.question: In a ΔABC, the sides are AB = 16 cm, AC = 63 cm, BC = 65 cm. From A, a straight line AM is drawn up to the midpoint M of side BC. Then the length of AM is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: In a ΔABC, the sides are AB = 16 cm, AC = 63 cm, BC = 65 cm. From A, a straight line AM is drawn up to the midpoint M of side BC. Then the length of AM is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Using Apollonius theorem, we know that

⇒ 2(AM2 + BM2) = AB2 + AC2

⇒ 2[AM2 + (65/2)2] = 162 + 632

⇒ 2[AM2 + (4225/4)] = 256 + 3969

⇒ AM2 = 2112.5 – 1056.25

questions.question: In circle with centre O, AB is a diameter and CD is a chord such that ABCD is a trapezium. If ∠BAC = 15°, then ∠CAD is equal to
questions.questionHtml: In circle with centre O, AB is a diameter and CD is a chord such that ABCD is a trapezium. If ∠BAC = 15°, then ∠CAD is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, ∠BAC = 15°

⇒ ∠ACB = 90° [Angle in a semicircle is 90]

In ΔACB

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠CBA + ∠BAC = 180°

⇒ ∠CBA = 180° – 90° – 15° = 75°

⇒ ∠DCA = ∠CAB = 15° [Alternate interior angle]

⇒ ∠DCA = ∠ABD = 15° and ∠CAD = ∠DBC

∵ Two inscribed angles forming the same arc or forming two equal arcs are equal.

⇒ ∠CBA = ∠DBC + ∠ABD

⇒ 75° = ∠DBC + 15°

⇒ ∠DBC = 75° – 15° = 60°

⇒ ∠CAD = ∠DBC = 60°

questions.solution:
Let radius of sphere be r cm

Volume of sphere = [4/3] × π r3

If radius increased by 140%

New radius of sphere = r × [240/100] = 2.4r

New volume of sphere = [4/3] × π × (2.4r)3 = [4/3] × π × 13.824 × r3

Volume increased by = \(\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\pi }} \times {\rm{}}13.824{{\rm{r}}^3} - {\rm{\;}}\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}{\rm{}} = {\rm{}}\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}\left( {13.824 - 1} \right){\rm{}} = {\rm{}}12.824{\rm{}} \times {\rm{}}\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}\)

∴ Required percentage = \(\left[ {\frac{{12.824{\rm{\;}} \times {\rm{\;}}\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}}}{{\frac{4}{3}{\rm{\pi }}{{\rm{r}}^3}}}} \right]{\rm{}} \times {\rm{}}100 = 1282.4\% \)

questions.question: A train without stoppage travels with an average speed of 70 km/h, and with stoppage, it travels with the average speed of 56 km/h. How many minutes, does the train stop on an average per hour?

questions.solution:
Without stoppage average speed = 70 km/h

With stoppages average speed = 56 km/h

As we know,

Time of rest per hour equal to the difference in average speed divided by the speed without stoppage.

∴ Required time = [(70 – 56)/70] × 60 = 12

questions.question: If (3x – 1) 3 + (4x – 3) 3 + (2x + 1) 3 = 3(3x – 1)(4x – 3)(2x + 1) and x ≠ 1/3, then x = ?

questions.solution:
If a3 + b3 + c3 – 3abc = 0, then

a + b + c = 0 or a = b = c

⇒ (3x – 1)3 + (4x – 3)3 + (2x + 1)3 = 3(3x – 1) (4x – 3) (2x + 1)

⇒ (3x – 1)3 + (4x – 3)3 + (2x + 1)3 – 3(3x – 1) (4x – 3) (2x + 1) = 0

Using the above formula, 

⇒ (3x – 1) = (4x – 3) 

⇒ 3x – 1 = 4x – 3

⇒ – 1  + 3 = 4x – 3x

⇒ x = 2

questions.question: The value of 3.8 – (4.2 ÷ 0.7 × 3) + 5 × 2 ÷ 0.5 is∶
questions.questionHtml: The value of 3.8 – (4.2 ÷ 0.7 × 3) + 5 × 2 ÷ 0.5 is∶
questions.solution:
Follow BODMAS rule to solve this question, as per the order given below ∶

Step-1 ∶ Parts of an equation enclosed in 'Brackets' must be solved first, and in the bracket,

Step-2 ∶ Any mathematical 'Of' or 'Exponent' must be solved next,

Step-3 ∶ Next, the parts of the equation that contain 'Division' and 'Multiplication' are calculated,

Step-4 ∶ Last but not least, the parts of the equation that contain 'Addition' and 'Subtraction' should be calculated.

⇒ 3.8 – (4.2 ÷ 0.7 × 3) + 5 × 2 ÷ 0.5

⇒ 3.8 – (6 × 3) + 5 × 4

⇒ 3.8 – 18 + 20

⇒ 23.8 – 18

⇒ 5.8

questions.question: The price of sugar is increased by 18%. A person wants to increase the expenditure by 12% only. By what percent, correct to one decimal place, should he decrease his consumption?
questions.questionHtml: The price of sugar is increased by 18%. A person wants to increase the expenditure by 12% only. By what percent, correct to one decimal place, should he decrease his consumption?
questions.solution:
Let the initial price of sugar be 100x.

Price of sugar after increased = 100x × [118/100] = 118x

Person wants his expenditure increase by 12% only,

So, his expenditure should be = 100x × [112/100] = 112x

∴ Required percentage = [(118 – 112x)/118] × 100 = 5.08% ≈ 5.1%

questions.question: In ΔABC, AD is median and G is the point on AD such that AG ∶ GD = 2 ∶ 1. Then ar (ΔABG) ∶ ar(ΔABC) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, AD is median and G is the point on AD such that AG ∶ GD = 2 ∶ 1. Then ar (ΔABG) ∶ ar(ΔABC) is equal to:
questions.solution:
As we know,

AD is median, so AD divides triangle in two equal parts.

Ar ΔADB = Ar ΔADC

In ΔABD

⇒ Ar ΔBDG/Ar ΔBGA = DG/AG

⇒ Ar ΔBDG/ar ΔBGA = 1/2

Let the area of ΔBDG be 1 unit.

So, area of ΔBGA will be = 2 unit

So, area of ΔBAD = Ar ΔBDG + Ar ΔBGA = 1 + 2 = 3 unit

Area of ΔABC = 2 × Ar ΔBAD = 2 × 3 = 6 unit

∴ Ar ΔABG ∶ Ar ΔABC = 2 ∶ 6 = 1 ∶ 3

questions.question: If 2 sin 2 θ = 3 cos θ, and 0 ≤ θ < 90°, then θ = ?
questions.questionHtml: If 2 sin<sup>2</sup>θ = 3 cos θ, and 0 ≤ θ < 90°, then θ = ?
questions.solution:
If 2sin2θ = 3cosθ

⇒ 2(1 – cos2θ) = 3cosθ

⇒ 2cos2θ + 3cosθ – 2 = 0

⇒ 2cos2θ + 4cosθ – cosθ – 2 = 0

⇒ 2cosθ(cosθ + 2) – 1(cosθ + 2) = 0

⇒ (2cosθ – 1) (cosθ + 2) = 0

⇒ 2cosθ – 1 = 0

⇒ cosθ = 1/2

⇒ cosθ = cos60°

⇒ θ = 60°

Short trick

Put θ = 60°

⇒ 2 × (√3/2)2 = 3 × 1/2

⇒ 3/2 = 3/2 (Satisfied)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. REPUDIATE
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

REPUDIATE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'renounce'.

Key Points

  • The word 'repudiate' refers to refuse to accept or be associated with. It involves denying the truth or validity of something. ('अस्वीकार करना'.)
    • Example: The politician repudiated the allegations of corruption levied against him.
  • The word 'renounce' means to formally declare one's abandonment of a claim, right, or possession. It is a voluntary act and does not necessarily imply that the renunciation is unwilling or forced. ('त्याग करना'.)
    • Example: The king renounced his throne for his love of a common woman.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'. 

Additional Information

  • 'regret' means to feel sad or sorry about something that happened or was done, particularly a lost opportunity. ('पछतावा'.)
  • 'enforce' means to make people obey a rule or law. ('लागू करना'.)
  • 'sanction' implies official permission or approval for an action. ('मंजूरी'.)

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Soon, ﬂames ignited the wooden beams of the grand palace built by Xerxes. B. Men and women holding ﬂaming torches aloft raced up and down the palace terraces. C. When the ﬁre died out, all that remained of the magniﬁcent palace were the stone columns. D. Looters fought off the heat of the inferno to drag out gold and silver vessels.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. Soon, ﬂames ignited the wooden beams of the grand palace built by Xerxes.

B. Men and women holding ﬂaming torches aloft raced up and down the palace terraces.

C. When the ﬁre died out, all that remained of the magniﬁcent palace were the stone columns.

D. Looters fought off the heat of the inferno to drag out gold and silver vessels.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'BADC'.
 
Key Points
  • Sentence B introduces the scene where men and women are holding flaming torches, suggesting some kind of activity or event that involves fire.
  • Sentence A logically follows B because it shows where the fire from the torches ended up, igniting the wooden beams of the grand palace built by Xerxes.
  • Sentence D then follows as it describes another action that happens during the fire - looters dragging out gold and silver vessels amidst the heat of the inferno.
  • Finally, sentence C brings a conclusion to the occurrence, describing the end result - the remainder of the palace after the fire has died out are the stone columns.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. It was very unusual as boys were not supposed to be out of school at this late hour. B. He moved closer to the boy in anger so that he could recognise the miscreant and punish him. C. He felt angry as teachers ought to be about school rules being broken. D. Mr Oliver, the school teacher saw a lonely boy sitting on a rock, weeping soundlessly.
questions.questionHtml:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.

A. It was very unusual as boys were not supposed to be out of school at this late hour.

B. He moved closer to the boy in anger so that he could recognise the miscreant and punish him.

C. He felt angry as teachers ought to be about school rules being broken.

D. Mr Oliver, the school teacher saw a lonely boy sitting on a rock, weeping soundlessly.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'DACB'.
 
Key Points
  • The most logical order to arrange these sentences is to start with Mr. Oliver seeing a boy, as mentioned in sentence D.
  • Sentence A follows naturally from D, explaining the unusualness of the situation, that the boy was out of school at a late hour.
  • Sentence C then explains Mr. Oliver's anger resulting from rules being broken.
  • Finally, sentence B concludes the paragraph by showing Mr. Oliver's decision, moving closer to recognise and punish the boy.
Therefore, the correct order is 'Option 2'.
 
Additional Information
  • The other options do not present the sequence of events in a way that seems logical or following a proper narrative progression. They start in the middle of the story or leave the conclusion in between, making the story unintelligible and disjointed.
